newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine senator says alliance to respect peg.
newsitem.headline: Argentine senator says alliance to respect peg.

text.p: One of the leaders of a powerful new Argentine political alliance on Monday said it did not oppose the government's current policy of pegging the value of the peso at par with the dollar, a news report said.

Sen. Graciela Fernandez Meijide said her center-left Frepaso party and the centrist Radicals, which announced the formation of a new alliance on Sunday, would respect the so-called Convertibility currency policy.
In October's midterm elections, Meijide will head the alliance's list of candidates seeking to represent the key Buenos Aires province in the lower chamber of Congress.
Mejide said "economists from the Radicals and Frepaso will start to analyze common proposals, respecting Convertibility," according to state-run news agency Telam.
The government of Peronist President Carlos Menem introduced Convertibility in 1991, pegging the value of the peso to the dollar at par and helping Argentina reduce inflation to zero.
Meijide said the alliance would not meddle with that policy because of "a very ingrained fear" of hyper-inflation among Argentines.
She added that "the idea that Convertibility acts like a corset on exports has been disproved."
"Only when popular fears of instability have disappeared will it (Convertibility) be modified," said Meijide.

Political analysts said the formation of Frepaso-Radical alliance has completely altered the Argentine political panorama, with the Peronists no longer guaranteed a majority in the lower house of Congress after the October elections. It has also raised the possibililty that Menem's successor as president in 1999 will come from outside the Peronist ranks.
